how: Kept by hand. One question a day on the Today tab, taken in order and starting again after the last. Each has q (the question), a (two to four answers), c (which answer is right, counting from 0), why (one line shown afterwards) and optionally id (an Explore card to open). Every answer must be backed by a card in Explore or an entry in onthisday.json. kids is a second list in the same shape, with easier questions for children: the card has a link to switch.

questions.q: In what year did the first Portuguese families arrive in Bermuda aboard the Golden Rule?
questions.why: 58 men, women and children came from Madeira on 4 November 1849.

questions.q: How many people from the American brig Enterprise chose freedom in Bermuda in 1835?
questions.why: 78 were aboard. 72 chose to stay and be free.

questions.q: Who made the bronzes We Arrive and When Voices Rise in Hamilton?
questions.why: Both are by the Bermudian sculptor Chesley Trott.

questions.q: About how long did the Theatre Boycott of 1959 take to end segregated seating in the cinemas?
questions.why: It began on 15 June and the cinemas reopened integrated on 2 July.

questions.q: What was the secret group that organised the 1959 Theatre Boycott called?
questions.why: Its members kept their names hidden for years afterwards.

questions.q: About how many convicts did Britain send to Bermuda to build the Dockyard?
questions.why: About 9,000 came between 1824 and 1863, and some 2,000 died here.

questions.q: Where did most of the convicts who built the Dockyard sleep?
questions.why: Seven prison hulks were moored off the works over the years.

questions.q: Which ship left Portsmouth in January 1824 with the first 300 convicts for Bermuda?
questions.why: Antelope sailed on 5 January 1824.

questions.q: What were the round stone buildings in the seawall at Boaz Island built for?
a: Convicts to bathe in the sea
questions.why: They let convicts wash in the sea without a chance to escape.

questions.q: Which Bermuda town boomed during the American Civil War?
questions.why: Blockade runners used St George's as their base.

questions.q: During the American Civil War, where did the Confederate agent in Bermuda keep his office?
questions.why: Major Norman Walker worked from the Globe in St George's.

questions.q: About how many Boer prisoners of war were held in Bermuda?
questions.why: About 5,000, at a time when Bermuda had only about 17,000 people.

questions.q: Where in Bermuda were the Boer prisoners of war kept?
a: On islands in the Great Sound
questions.why: Darrell's, Burt, Tucker's, Morgan's, Hawkins and Hinson's islands all had camps.

questions.q: In the Second World War, which hotel housed more than a thousand British censors?
questions.why: The Princess was the headquarters of Imperial Censorship in the Atlantic.

questions.q: What were the women who examined wartime mail in Bermuda nicknamed?
questions.why: Many were chosen for their languages.

questions.q: What was hidden in Bermuda in 1944 so that Germany would not know its codes were lost?
questions.why: U-505 was towed in on 19 June 1944 and kept under guard.

questions.q: Where did Churchill, Eisenhower and the French premier meet in December 1953?
questions.why: The Big Three met at the Mid Ocean Club in Tucker's Town.

questions.q: Which American president met Harold Macmillan at Government House in December 1961?
questions.why: Kennedy landed at Kindley on 21 December 1961.

questions.q: Which two leaders met in Bermuda on Good Friday 1990?
questions.why: George Bush and Margaret Thatcher met at Government House on 13 April 1990.

questions.q: Where was Bermuda's first airport?
questions.why: Flying boats used Darrell's Island from 1937.

questions.q: How did the Royal Navy's great floating dock get to Bermuda?
a: It sailed under its own power
It came in pieces by steamer
It was towed across the Atlantic
questions.why: Two ironclads towed it across. Its frame still lies off Spanish Point.

questions.q: In which parish was Mary Prince born?
questions.why: She was born at Brackish Pond around 1788.

questions.q: In what year was The History of Mary Prince published?
questions.why: It went through three printings in its first year.

questions.q: On what date did slavery end in Bermuda?
questions.why: The first day of Cup Match is now Emancipation Day.

questions.q: In what year was the cricket match between Somerset and St George's first played for a cup?
questions.why: It grew out of the picnics that marked Emancipation.

questions.q: Who made the statue of Sally Bassett at the Cabinet Office?
questions.why: It was officially commemorated on 9 February 2009.

questions.q: Who was Bermuda's first National Hero?
questions.why: She was named in October 2008.

questions.q: How many National Heroes does Bermuda have?
questions.why: The eighth, Sir John Swan, was named in 2016.

questions.q: When is National Heroes Day?
questions.why: It honours the eight people officially named National Heroes.

questions.q: Which African name did Dr E.F. Gordon take in 1947?
questions.why: He announced it on 22 June 1947 as a protest.

questions.q: Who was Bermuda's longest serving Premier?
questions.why: He was also the first National Hero named in his lifetime.

questions.q: In what year was Bermuda's first general election with one equal vote for every adult?
questions.why: 19,123 people voted, 91 per cent of those registered.

questions.q: In what year was the Vasco da Gama Club founded?
questions.why: It began as a benefit society for its members.

questions.q: In what year did Bermuda switch to the dollar?
questions.why: Decimal money arrived on 6 February 1970.

questions.q: The telegraph cable approved in 1889 linked Bermuda with which city?
questions.why: It was wanted for military, naval and colonial reasons.

questions.q: What did William Beebe use for his record dives off Nonsuch Island in the 1930s?
questions.why: A steel ball lowered on a cable, with Otis Barton beside him.

questions.q: Which bird, believed lost for centuries, was found alive in Bermuda in 1951?
questions.why: David Wingate was a schoolboy on the expedition that found it.

questions.q: How many ships did the Sea Venture survivors build to carry them on to Virginia in 1610?
questions.why: They sailed on 10 May 1610.

questions.q: Which Royal Navy ship was lost in the hurricane of October 1926?
questions.why: The hurricane killed 110 people, most of them in shipwrecks.

questions.q: What were Star Tiger and Star Ariel?
questions.why: They vanished in 1948 and 1949.

questions.q: Joseph Rainey cut hair in St George's during the American Civil War. What did he become?
a: The first Black member of the US House of Representatives
questions.why: His barber shop was in the kitchen of Tucker House.

questions.q: In what year did the United States close its bases in Bermuda?
questions.why: They closed on 1 September 1995.

questions.q: What was the Bermuda Conference of April 1943 called to discuss?
questions.why: It is remembered as a failure.

questions.q: Which Hamilton hotel opened on 1 January 1885?
questions.why: It was named for Princess Louise, who had visited two years earlier.

questions.q: In 1957 an MP told the House of Commons that only British cars were seen in Bermuda. Why?
a: American cars were too big for the law
questions.why: No American car was small enough to pass the island's rules.

questions.q: In what year was the closing of the Dockyard announced?
questions.why: The Commons was told on 3 May 1950.

questions.q: In which sport did Flora Duffy win Olympic gold for Bermuda?
questions.why: She was born on 30 September 1987.

questions.q: Which Irish nationalist was held in a Bermuda prison hulk in 1848?
questions.why: He wrote of being sealed up in a hulk, kept apart from the other prisoners.

questions.q: How did the enslaved pilot James Darrell win his freedom?
a: He bought it with prize money
He piloted an admiral's warship through the reefs
questions.why: He brought HMS Resolution to Murray's Anchorage in 1795 and was freed in 1796.

questions.q: In what year did Pilot James Darrell buy his house in St George's?
questions.why: He paid 50 pounds for it on 19 April 1800. His family still owns it.

questions.q: For how long did the organisers of the 1959 Theatre Boycott keep their names secret?
questions.why: The Progressive Group revealed their names in 1999.

questions.q: Where were the flyers for the 1959 Theatre Boycott printed?
questions.why: Gerald and Izola Harvey printed them at home.

questions.q: Where is the heart of Sir George Somers buried?
questions.why: His nephew buried it in what is now Somers Garden in 1610.

questions.q: Which Shakespeare play is the wreck of the Sea Venture believed to have inspired?
questions.why: Accounts of the wreck reached London in 1610.

questions.q: What date is carved on Portuguese Rock at Spittal Pond?
questions.why: It is the oldest sign of people in Bermuda, cut by shipwrecked sailors.

questions.q: Before the Causeway opened in 1871, how did people get to St George's?
a: Along a sandbar at low tide
questions.why: A ferry had run at Ferry Reach since 1622, and from the 1790s it carried horses too.

questions.q: What is Hog Bay named after?
questions.why: Spanish sailors left hogs on the island in the 1500s.

questions.q: What was the pond behind Somerset Long Bay beach before the Audubon Society restored it?
questions.why: The Society took it on in the early 1970s and brought the pond back.

questions.q: What is the Lost at Sea Memorial in St David's shaped like?
a: A rowing boat on its end
questions.why: Bill Ming cast it from a boat about a hundred years old.

questions.q: Whose sea chest is kept at the Bermuda Historical Society Museum?
questions.why: His flagship, the Sea Venture, was wrecked on Bermuda's reefs in 1609.

kids.q: What colour are the roofs of Bermuda's houses?
kids.why: The heavy white roofs help houses stand up to hurricanes and catch the rain.

kids.q: Long ago, prisoners who built the Dockyard slept in old warships. What were those ships called?
kids.why: There were seven of them over the years.

kids.q: How many bronze people are stepping ashore in the statue We Arrive?
kids.why: They stand for 72 people who chose to be free in 1835.

kids.q: What job did Joseph Rainey do in St George's before he became famous in America?
kids.why: Barber's Alley is named for him.

kids.q: In the war, people in a big pink hotel read letters to look for spies. Which hotel?
kids.why: More than a thousand people worked there.

kids.q: Which Bermuda bird was thought lost for hundreds of years and then found again?
kids.why: It was found in 1951.

kids.q: What did the pilot James Darrell steer safely through the reefs?
kids.why: The admiral was so pleased that he asked for him to be set free.

kids.q: Which ship was wrecked on Bermuda's reefs in 1609, the start of people living here?
kids.why: Everyone aboard got safely ashore.

kids.q: Bermuda's first airport was on an island. What kind of aeroplanes used it?
kids.why: They landed on the water at Darrell's Island.

kids.q: What is the name of the two day summer holiday with a famous cricket match?
kids.why: Its two days are Emancipation Day and Mary Prince Day.

kids.q: William Beebe went deep under the sea in a steel ball. What was it called?
kids.why: He dived off Nonsuch Island in the 1930s.

kids.q: In 1959 people stayed away from something for two weeks to make it fair for everyone. What was it?
kids.why: After two weeks everyone could sit where they liked.

kids.q: How many National Heroes does Bermuda have?
kids.why: National Heroes Day is the third Monday in June.

kids.q: Which town was Bermuda's first capital?
kids.why: It is full of old lanes and alleys.

kids.q: The round stone towers in the seawall at Boaz Island were for what?
kids.why: Convicts bathed there.

kids.q: Something enormous was towed all the way across the Atlantic to Bermuda by two warships. What was it?
kids.why: You can still see its rusty frame off Spanish Point.

kids.q: What is buried in Somers Garden in St George's?
a: The heart of Sir George Somers
kids.why: The rest of him was taken home to England.

kids.q: Who wrote a famous book about her own life after being born enslaved in Bermuda?
kids.why: It was published in London in 1831.

kids.q: Men from far away South Africa were once kept prisoner here. Where?
a: On small islands in the Great Sound
kids.why: There were about 5,000 of them.

kids.q: A captured submarine was once hidden in Bermuda. Which country had built it?
kids.why: It was called U-505.

kids.q: A rock by the sea at Spittal Pond is cracked into squares. What is it called?
kids.why: It looks like a giant game board.

kids.q: Long ago, what crossed the water at Ferry Reach on a boat, along with the people?
kids.why: The horse ferry carried horses and carriages to St George's.

kids.q: Why do people in Bermuda club together to buy ponds and woods?
kids.why: Once it is a nature reserve, nobody can build on it.

kids.q: Which giant insect sits in a fountain in Queen Elizabeth Park?
kids.why: It is a bronze sculpture, part of the sculpture garden.

kids.q: Bermuda's first coins are called hog money. Which animal is on them?
kids.why: Wild hogs ran all over the island when the first settlers came.
